claim_statement: Two distinct, approximately-linear, independently-recoverable directions in the residual stream: h (harmfulness perception) and r (refusal execution), at different positions.
variant_metric: partial: h-AUROC=1.000 (harmfulness), cos(h,r)=0.068 (ratio=0.069 of split-half 0.978); r-AUROC=NaN (refusal unmeasurable at high bare-refusal rate)
main_experiment_metric: partial: h-AUROC=0.9998, cos(h,r)=0.174 (ratio=0.20 of split-half 0.883); r-AUROC=NaN
delta: cosine ratio improved (0.069 vs 0.20 — h and r are even more geometrically distinct on Qwen2); h-AUROC +0.0002 (ceiling); refusal-side still NaN on Qwen2
reasoning: The variant verdict is 'partial' — same as the main experiment (partial maps to not-supported in the binary scheme). Qwen2-Instruct-7B replicates the core geometry finding: h direction cleanly separates harmful from benign at ceiling AUROC (1.000 at layer 15), and cos(h,r)=0.068 is even further below the 0.5×split-half threshold (cosine ratio 0.069 vs 0.20 in main experiment). The refusal-side sub-tests (AUROC_r_on_refusal and shuffled-r) remain NaN because Qwen2 also refuses almost all bare-harmful prompts (only 0 or 1 natural jailbreaks in 520 attempts). The independent-recoverability claim cannot be verified on either model with AdvBench bare-harmful prompts. claim_supported=fail (partial maps to not-supported, not unambiguously supported). consistent_with_main_experiment=pass because the main experiment's not-supported verdict is reproduced: flip(fail)=pass.
